verdict.rationale: Pipecat ships a first-party evals system, Pipecat Evals. You describe a conversation and the expected behavior, and it runs that against your real agent pipeline to check whether the expectation still holds. A runtime probe confirmed the official CLI exposes an `eval` command for behavioral evals. Evals run against the real agent and services rather than an isolated sandbox, but the story asks for pre-deployment simulated conversations and evals, not sandbox isolation. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of an eval run producing results, and detail on simulating telephony-specific audio/caller conditions or eval scoring depth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can test agents with simulated conversations or evals before putting them on real phone calls

citations.quote: Pipecat Evals is the framework's built-in system for testing agent behavior. You describe a conversation and the behavior you expect, and Pipecat runs it against your real agent
Pipecat runs it against your real agent (the same pipeline, the same services, the same code) and tells you whether the expectation still holds.
